subject: Unexpected latency and 5xxs on dedicated pool — ExaBay production
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@exabay.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: jane.porter@exabay.com
Date: Thu, 28 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected latency & 5xxs on dedicated pool - ExaBay production

Hi Kimberly —

We started seeing elevated tail latency and intermittent 5xx errors from our Redwood Dedicated endpoint around 08:50 PDT. Error rate climbed from ~0.2% to ~3.8% for our production traffic, p95 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~850ms, and some calls are timing out after retry. This is affecting our checkout and fraud-scoring flows.

Attached are a short set of logs and a span screenshot (kb-span.png) showing repeated KV cache misses. We are on the reserved capacity plan (DEAL-4783) and this is high-severity for us. Can you confirm whether this is a regional pool saturation or something on our config? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether we can get temporary capacity or a swift fallback.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Rao
Head of Platform, ExaBay
ops+platform@exabay.com

Team — looping you in. Short summary for context: ExaBay (DEAL-4783) is experiencing a production impact with p95 latency ~850ms and a spike in 5xx. They are on a reserved GPU pool in us-west. Samir attached logs indicating repeated KV cache evictions.

Immediate asks:
- Can Eng confirm whether the reserved pool for ExaBay is saturated / experiencing contention? (rishi)
- Ops: can we provision a temporary burst (reserved bump) for the next 12 hours while we stabilize? If provisioning is manual, please advise ETA. (priyom)
- CS/Sales: prepare a short executive note for ExaBay C-suite with proposed remediation and compensation (marissa)

Please treat this as high priority. Samir, we will update you within 30 minutes on next steps.

-Kim

Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & 5xxs on dedicated pool - ExaBay production

Kim / team — quick technical snapshot from the runtime side after an initial check:
- Observed high GPU utilization on the exabay-reserved-pool (pool-id: rp-3a9) starting ~08:45 PDT with continuous >98% GPU SM utilization on multiple hosts.
- KV cache churn increased significantly when sequence lengths spiked due to a downstream retry storm; cache evictions caused repeated recompute of KV which amplified token generation latency.
- We see a correlation with a higher fraction of long-sequence requests from the fraud-scoring model variant (gptx-fraud-large).

Immediate mitigations I'm pushing now:
1) Route 30% of traffic to the gptx-fraud-8bit variant (compatible) to reduce memory pressure and lower per-token compute.
2) Enable aggressive prefix caching for the next 2 hours for this tenant only.
3) Requesting a temporary burst allocation (+2 GPU workers) to rp-3a9; ops, please confirm feasibility.

If routing and cache changes reduce the tail, we can avoid a bigger capacity bump. If not, we'll escalate to a short-term reserved bump while we implement a longer-term quantization+batching profile for them.

Attaching a short CSV of pool metrics for the window (pool-metrics-20271028.csv).

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE, Serving Runtime

Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: ExaBay dedicated pool incident: immediate remediation and next steps

Samir / Jane —

First, I want to apologize for the disruption this week. We understand how critical the checkout and fraud flows are and take this seriously. Below is what we've implemented and what you'll see in the next 72 hours.

What we did (completed):
- Immediately routed 30% of fraud-scoring traffic to the 8-bit compatible model variant. This reduced memory pressure and has already moved p95 down to ~210ms in controlled tests.
- Enabled tenant-only aggressive prefix/KV caching for ExaBay for the next 24 hours.
- Provisioned a temporary +2 GPU burst allocation for your reserved pool (rp-3a9) for the next 12 hours; ops confirmed availability at 11:10 PDT yesterday.

Next steps (72-hour plan):
- Today: run a controlled canary ramp of the fallback variant to 50% over 3 hours and monitor error budget.
- 24-48h: apply model quantization profile and updated batching policy recommended by Eng to reduce per-token cost and pressure.
- 48-72h: schedule a joint post-incident review (PIR) to review root causes, commit to a permanent config change, and align on any contractual adjustments.

Compensation: we will credit one week of token usage on the impacted service tier while we execute the remediation plan; Marissa will prepare formal wording and approval.

Executive offer: if the SLA threshold is breached again in the next 30 days, we'd like to offer a 1:1 sync between our CTO (or myself) and ExaBay's platform exec to align on capacity and architecture.

Please let us know if you need an immediate bridge or prefer the PIR to be scheduled after we complete the 72-hour plan. We will keep you updated every 3 hours during the immediate window.

Thanks for your patience and partnership — we will get this stable.

Best,
Kim
